# kind=host_not_in_cohort   db_v3 plant species the four-cereal cohort no longer needs
# kind=ploidy_redundant     held purely as a second ploidy, costing k-mers to the genus node

# kind=no_assembly          named by a cereal leaf survey but nothing exists to build from
# kind=synonym_already_held the taxon is in the database under its current name
# kind=out_of_scope         excluded by a scope decision, not by availability

column4: reason

FUNGI-ONLY PAPER, Leon's call 2026-10-13. db_v3 holds 29 oomycete species / 185 M minimizers (3.8% of the database); all come out. Costs nothing measurable: ZERO of those 29 pass both 05_filter floors on any cereal host, so no cereal detection depends on them. It also removes a holobase problem rather than inheriting it, since holobase holds no oomycete assemblies at all and the 738 plant-associated oomycete taxa USDA records would each have needed resolving against NCBI (CLAUDE.md active task 5). CLAUDE.md's Scope section still says "fungi and oomycetes" and must be updated.

A PLANT in the fungal seed list. USDA's fungus column is not strictly fungi: it legitimately records plant parasites as "recorded on" a host. Caught because Capsicum was being selected as an addable reference with 6 annotated assemblies. build_seeds.py now filters tf.kingdom='Fungi'.
Broomrape, a parasitic plant. Same cause as Capsicum annuum above.

durum. 27.7% of the Triticum clade's 51.8M minimizers sit at the GENUS node because db_v3 holds both hexaploid aestivum and tetraploid turgidum, so a correct wheat call can score low coverage. Dropping it moves those k-mers to the species node. Nothing in the chapter distinguishes durum from bread wheat, so it costs nothing.
2,084,086 minimizers. Host of the 02_literature cohort, not the four-cereal one.

Hemiptera. The FUNGUS is 5206. The datasets CLI refuses the bare name 'Cryptococcus' and datasets_query() returned [] on the non-zero exit, so the clade silently selected nothing: cost 36 assemblies / 14 species before it was caught. Always seed this genus by taxid.
Coleoptera, Monotomidae. The FUNGUS (arbuscular mycorrhizal) is 1129544. Same silent-zero failure as Cryptococcus: cost 6 assemblies / 3 species.

Old name for Pyricularia, which the database holds (P. oryzae, 109 cereal detections). Zero assemblies exist under the old name, so Dastogeer 2022 naming it as a rice leaf genus is a nomenclature artefact, not a gap. Do NOT add.

P. nodorum is a synonym of Parastagonospora nodorum, which the database holds. Yin 2023's rice core 'Phaeosphaeria 4.5%' may therefore be an organism already present. CHECK WHICH SPECIES before adding; this row is a caution, not a settled exclusion.
